caption: Figure 2: Node graphs of 1D representations of architectures commonly used in medical imaging. a) Auto-encoder, b) restricted Boltzmann machine, c) recurrent neural network, d) convolutional neural network, e) multi-stream convolutional neural network, f) U-net (with a single downsampling stage).
description:
Figure type: Diagrammatic representation of various neural network architectures.
Description: The figure illustrates six different types of neural network architectures commonly used in medical imaging. Each panel (a-f) represents a distinct architecture: a) Auto-encoder, b) Restricted Boltzmann machine, c) Recurrent neural network, d) Convolutional neural network, e) Multi-stream convolutional neural network, f) U-net with a single downsampling stage. The nodes and connections are color-coded to indicate different types of nodes and connections.

Text in figure: Auto-encoder, Restricted Boltzmann machine, Recurrent neural network, Convolutional neural network, Multi-stream convolutional neural network, U-net, Input node, Hidden node, Output node, Probabilistic node, Pooling connection, Weighted connection, Down-sample, Up-sample, Concatenate, Up-convolution.

caption: Figure 3: Collage of some medical imaging applications in which deep learning has achieved state-of-the-art results. From top-left to bottom-right: mammographic mass classification (Kooi et al., 2016), segmentation of lesions in the brain (top ranking in BRATS, ISLES and MRBrains challenges, image from Ghafoorian et al. (2016b), leak detection in airway tree segmentation (Charbonnier et al., 2017), diabetic retinopathy classification (Kaggle Diabetic Retinopathy challenge 2015, image from van Grinsven et al. (2016), prostate segmentation (top rank in PROMISE12 challenge), nodule classification (top ranking in LUNA16 challenge), breast cancer metastases detection in lymph nodes (top ranking and human expert performance in CAMELYON16), human expert performance in skin lesion classification (Esteva et al., 2017), and state-of-the-art bone suppression in x-rays, image from Yang et al. (2016c).
description:
## Description
This figure is a collage showcasing various medical imaging applications where deep learning has achieved state-of-the-art results. Each panel represents a different application, including mammographic mass classification, brain lesion segmentation, airway tree segmentation, diabetic retinopathy classification, prostate segmentation, nodule classification, breast cancer metastases detection, skin lesion classification, and bone suppression in x-rays.
